title: Impact of COPS Grant on Violent Crime Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (municipality and period).
- Why: We observe municipalities over time with some receiving COPS hiring grants (treated) and others not, plus pre- and post-allocation periods. DID exploits within-municipality changes relative to untreated municipalities over the same periods.
- Estimand: ATT of COPS grant on log violent crime rate. In logs, the coefficient translates to a percent change: 100*(exp(beta) − 1).
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of grants, treated and control municipalities would have followed similar trends in violent crime.
  - No spillovers: Treatment in one municipality does not affect outcomes in others.
  - Stable composition and no differential measurement changes across groups over time.
  - If treatment is staggered, TWFE DID is interpreted as a weighted average of cohort-time effects; we check dynamics with an event-study and add unit-specific linear trends as robustness.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages (install if missing)
pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest", "sandwich", "lmtest")
to_install <- pkgs[!pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
if(length(to_install) > 0){
  install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s46_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# Ensure expected columns exist
stopifnot(all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(dt)))

# Basic checks
dt[, unit_id := as.integer(unit_id)]
dt[, period  := as.integer(period)]
dt[, treated := as.integer(treated)]
dt[, post    := as.integer(post)]
dt[, treat_x_post := as.integer(treat_x_post)]
dt[, y := as.numeric(y)]

# Sanity check: treat_x_post should equal treated * post
if(any(dt$treat_x_post != dt$treated * dt$post, na.rm = TRUE)){
  warning("treat_x_post is not equal to treated * post for some rows.")
}

# 2) Main DID: Two-way fixed effects, cluster by municipality
mod_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = "unit_id")
ct_twfe <- summary(mod_twfe)$coeftable
beta <- unname(ct_twfe["treat_x_post","Estimate"])
se   <- unname(ct_twfe["treat_x_post","Std. Error"])
pval <- unname(ct_twfe["treat_x_post","Pr(>t)"])
ci_lo <- beta - 1.96*se
ci_hi <- beta + 1.96*se
pct_change <- 100*(exp(beta)-1)

cat("MAIN RESULT: TWFE DID\n")
cat(sprintf("  Beta (treat_x_post): %.4f\n  SE (clustered by unit): %.4f\n  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n  p-value: %.4f\n  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n",
            beta, se, ci_lo, ci_hi, pval, pct_change))

# 3) Robustness A: Simple 2x2 DID without FE (controls for levels and common time)
mod_2x2 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = dt)
vc_2x2 <- sandwich::vcovCL(mod_2x2, cluster = dt$unit_id)
ct_2x2 <- lmtest::coeftest(mod_2x2, vcov = vc_2x2)
beta_2x2 <- unname(ct_2x2["treat_x_post","Estimate"])
se_2x2   <- unname(ct_2x2["treat_x_post","Std. Error"])
ci_lo_2x2 <- beta_2x2 - 1.96*se_2x2
ci_hi_2x2 <- beta_2x2 + 1.96*se_2x2
pct_change_2x2 <- 100*(exp(beta_2x2)-1)

cat("ROBUSTNESS A: Simple DID (no FE), cluster by unit\n")
cat(sprintf("  Beta (treat_x_post): %.4f\n  SE: %.4f\n  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n",
            beta_2x2, se_2x2, ci_lo_2x2, ci_hi_2x2, pct_change_2x2))

# 4) Robustness B: TWFE + unit-specific linear trends
#    Uses fixest's fslope() for municipality-specific linear time trends
mod_trend <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period + fslope(period, unit_id),
                   data = dt, cluster = "unit_id")
ct_trend <- summary(mod_trend)$coeftable
beta_tr  <- unname(ct_trend["treat_x_post","Estimate"])
se_tr    <- unname(ct_trend["treat_x_post","Std. Error"])
ci_lo_tr <- beta_tr - 1.96*se_tr
ci_hi_tr <- beta_tr + 1.96*se_tr
pct_change_tr <- 100*(exp(beta_tr)-1)

cat("ROBUSTNESS B: TWFE + unit-specific linear trends, cluster by unit\n")
cat(sprintf("  Beta (treat_x_post): %.4f\n  SE: %.4f\n  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n",
            beta_tr, se_tr, ci_lo_tr, ci_hi_tr, pct_change_tr))

# 5) Event-study for dynamics and pre-trend diagnostic (relative to t = -1)
#    Compute first treatment period (cohort) for each treated municipality
cohort_dt <- dt[treated == 1 & post == 1, .(cohort = min(period)), by = unit_id]
dt <- merge(dt, cohort_dt, by = "unit_id", all.x = TRUE)
dt[, rel_time := ifelse(!is.na(cohort), period - cohort, NA_integer_)]

# Event-study using i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1)
es_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = "unit_id")

# Extract event-time coefficients
es_sum <- summary(es_mod)
cn <- rownames(es_sum$coeftable)
is_es <- grepl("^i\\(rel_time,treated\\)::", cn)
es_names <- cn[is_es]
# Parse event times, robust to parentheses for negatives
ev_t <- as.numeric(gsub(".*::\\(?(-?\\d+)\\)?$", "\\1", es_names, perl = TRUE))
es_est <- es_sum$coeftable[is_es, "Estimate"]
es_se  <- es_sum$coeftable[is_es, "Std. Error"]
es_df  <- data.table(event_time = ev_t, estimate = es_est, se = es_se)

# Pre-trend check: average of leads at t <= -2
pre_leads <- es_df[event_time <= -2]
avg_pre <- if(nrow(pre_leads) > 0) mean(pre_leads$estimate) else NA_real_

# Short-run post effect: average of t in [0, 2]
post_window <- es_df[event_time >= 0 & event_time <= 2]
avg_post <- if(nrow(post_window) > 0) mean(post_window$estimate) else NA_real_
avg_post_pct <- 100*(exp(avg_post)-1)

cat("EVENT-STUDY DIAGNOSTIC (ref = t = -1), cluster by unit\n")
if(!is.na(avg_pre)){
  cat(sprintf("  Avg pre-trend (t <= -2): %.4f (should be ~0 under parallel trends)\n", avg_pre))
} else {
  cat("  Avg pre-trend (t <= -2): not available (insufficient pre-periods)\n")
}
if(!is.na(avg_post)){
  cat(sprintf("  Avg short-run post effect (t in [0,2]): %.4f (%.2f%%)\n\n", avg_post, avg_post_pct))
} else {
  cat("  Avg short-run post effect (t in [0,2]): not available\n\n")
}

# 6) Robustness C: Two-way clustering (unit and period) on the main TWFE
mod_twfe_2wc <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = c("unit_id","period"))
ct_twfe_2wc <- summary(mod_twfe_2wc)$coeftable
beta_2wc <- unname(ct_twfe_2wc["treat_x_post","Estimate"])
se_2wc   <- unname(ct_twfe_2wc["treat_x_post","Std. Error"])
ci_lo_2wc <- beta_2wc - 1.96*se_2wc
ci_hi_2wc <- beta_2wc + 1.96*se_2wc
pct_change_2wc <- 100*(exp(beta_2wc)-1)

cat("ROBUSTNESS C: TWFE with two-way clustering (unit and period)\n")
cat(sprintf("  Beta (treat_x_post): %.4f\n  SE (2-way clustered): %.4f\n  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n",
            beta_2wc, se_2wc, ci_lo_2wc, ci_hi_2wc, pct_change_2wc))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. COPS hiring grants should reduce violent crime by increasing sworn officer staffing and deterrence.
- Magnitude: A modest but meaningful reduction. I expect a DID coefficient between −0.05 and −0.12 on log violent crime, implying roughly 5% to 11% lower violent crime in treated municipalities after grant allocation. Effects may grow over 1–2 years post-award in the event study (implementation lag), with pre-trends close to zero. Robustness checks (unit trends, alternative SEs) should yield similar magnitudes.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in violent crime rates between municipalities that received the grant and those that did not, before and after the grant allocation.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis reveals a positive effect of the COPS grant on the violent crime rate.
